articles.description:
ffmpeg can find the cuts in an edited video with one filter, and most guides stop there: select='gt(scene,0.4)',showinfo, read the timestamps, done. On a real edit two things are still open afterwards. Which threshold separates cuts from camera shake, and how do you turn the timestamps into files that actually start on the cut? The video editor in the osFoundry desktop app does the first half in Rust (canvas_scene_split in canvas_operations.rs) and avoids the second half entirely. Below, both halves are rebuilt in Python and measured on one video, with the numbers that decide each choice.
The test file is NASA's public-domain launch highlights from the Artemis II test flight: 92 seconds of H.264 at 640×360, 30 fps, 2,760 frames, cut from 19 shots. All timings are from an Apple M1 with ffmp…
articles.title: How to find scene cuts with ffmpeg and split the video exactly on them

FreeToken is an open-source serving engine for running frontier-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models on personal and consumer hardware. Instead of assuming a datacenter GPU with room for every weight, it treats the GPU, the CPU, system memory and the links between them as one elastic inference platform, and it exposes OpenAI and Anthropic compatible APIs so coding agents can use a local model the way they use a cloud one.
It comes from FlashML-org, and the accompanying paper, "FreeToken: Efficie…

articles.description:
Last month I spent a Saturday afternoon cleaning up my aunt’s laptop, and it turned into one of the more interesting security conversations I’ve had all year. Nothing dramatic happened, no malware popup, no ransom note. It was just the small stuff: three antivirus trials fighting each other, a browser with too many extensions, and a Downloads folder that looked like a landfill.
I’ve noticed that helping relatives with tech is its own strange exercise. At work I can run a scan, check policy settings, maybe pull logs if something looks off. At her kitchen table I had none of that, and honestly I didn’t need most of it.

Here’s what struck me most: her laptop held more sensitive material than I expected. Tax documents from years back, scans of her passport, a folder of passwords she kept in a…
articles.title: What Fixing My Aunt’s Laptop Taught Me About Data Boundaries at Home

articles.author: senthil kumar
articles.description:
As founders, we spend countless hours building products, fixing bugs, and talking to customers. But when it comes to marketing, things get complicated quickly.
You need to research competitors, find keywords, write blog posts, create content for LinkedIn and X, engage on Reddit, optimize SEO, generate leads, and keep everything consistent. Most founders either spend too much time on marketing or can't afford a dedicated team.
That's why I built Marlo.
What is Marlo?
Marlo is an open-source AI CMO that helps founders and startups automate marketing research, strategy, and execution.
Instead of using multiple tools, Marlo combines everything into one platform powered by specialized AI agents.
What Marlo Can Do
Most AI marketing tools are black boxes.
I wanted Marlo to be:
Open and transparent
You own your data, choose your models, and extend the platform based on your needs.
Who Is Marlo For?
My vision is simple:
Every founder should have access to an AI-powered marketing team without paying agency prices or juggling dozens of disconnected tools.
Marlo is still evolving, and I'm actively looking for feedback from builders, marketers, and early adopters.
If you're interested in AI-powered growth, open-source software, or marketing automation, I'd love to hear your thoughts.
🚀 Try Marlo: https://marlo.mlforge.in
⭐ GitHub: https://github.com/Kumar2421/marlo-self-hosted-ai-cmo
articles.title: Building Marlo: An Open-Source AI CMO for Founders and Startups

articles.description:
"Done." It's probably the most satisfying word in a coding-agent session.
It can also conceal three very different questions:
Was the work permitted?
Did the work actually happen?
Did the result achieve what we needed?
All three matter. A single green checkmark can make them look like one decision.
Imagine asking a coding agent to update validation logic under src/**.
It edits the code, reports that its tests passed, and declares the task complete. Everything looks fine until you ask what the status actually proves.
The task was assigned to an implementer with a declared src/** write scope. But did the runtime enforce that scope for the tools the agent used?
The plan called for independent review. But who actually reviewed the final revision, and was that the revision ultimately merged?
Th…
articles.title: When an AI Agent Says 'Done,' What Exactly Has Finished?

To create a digital cassette on www.hearfromyou.xyz, open the submit page, write your message, add a title and the name of the person it's for, pick one to six tracks, style the tape, and publish it. Once it's live, it appears in a public archive that anyone can browse.
